Federal prosecutors issued grand jury subpoenas to Los Angeles County election officials regarding ballot handling. Registrar Dean Logan called the legal pressure an "intimidation" tactic, citing a "confrontational, adversarial approach" by federal officials.

summary: On Friday, the 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 2-1 to maintain a stay on a lower court's order, allowing Idaho to enforce its Defense of Life Act while the state's appeal proceeds.

Challenging the state's Defense of Life Act, Dr. Stacy Seyb of the St. Luke's Health System filed a lawsuit arguing the U.S. Constitution protects abortions when medically necessary to protect maternal health.

Circuit Judge Kim Wardlaw and Circuit Judge Consuelo Callahan wrote that Seyb is "unlikely to prevail," while Circuit Judge Marsha Berzon dissented, warning that "some women with serious pregnancy complications will...be required to continue their pregnancies at serious, permanent risk to their health."

Idaho Attorney General Raul Labrador applauded the ruling in a statement, asserting that "Idaho's unwavering protection for unborn children and their mothers will continue as intended" while the legal battle remains ongoing.

Stephanie Toti of the Lawyering Project called the decision a temporary setback, stating her team will demonstrate that "access to medically indicated abortion care is deeply rooted in our nation's history and tradition.
title: US court lifts ruling requiring Idaho to allow some abortions to protect women's health

summary: On Friday, federal prosecutors in Detroit unsealed a new indictment charging four additional individuals in an alleged conspiracy targeting University of Michigan leadership to force divestment from Israel.
This development brings the total number of charged defendants to 12, following an initial indictment five months ago that targeted eight activists for threats and property vandalism.

The new defendants include Henry David MacKeen-Shapiro, Aaron Hunter Vonbargen, Joseph Mark Fisher, and Srishti Tarana Sharma, accused of orchestrating terror campaigns against school officials and businesses.
U.S. Attorney Jerome Gorgon announced that two suspects were arrested and will make their first court appearances today, while authorities continue searching for the remaining two individuals.
Investigators previously linked the group to incidents including fake corpses placed in a board member's yard and spray-painting at the residence of former school president Santa Ono.
title: 4 more activists charged in intimidation campaign against University of Michigan over Israel ties

summary: On Friday, a prosecutor in Ohio dropped charges against Eljay Crisp-Carr, who was arrested following a June shooting that wounded 12 people at a neighborhood street festival.
The gunfire erupted June 6 during the Old West End Festival in Toledo, where a fight between rival groups escalated into a shooting in a neighborhood dotted with Victorian homes.

In September, Lucas County prosecuting attorney Julia Bates informed Crisp-Carr's attorney of discovery "that may support his defense," supporting defense attorney Alex Bodiford's argument that police arrested the wrong man.
A judge dismissed the charges without prejudice, meaning prosecutors retain legal authority to refile charges, while The Toledo Police Department continues its investigation.
Another defendant charged in the shooting remains in jail and is scheduled for a court appearance on Nov. 9, as the investigation persists.
title: Prosecutor Drops Charges Against Man Arrested in Ohio Festival Shooting that Wounded 12

summary: Pope Leo XIV addressed 'The Future of AI: A Dialogue Between the Vatican and the Scientific World on the Developments and Applications of Intelligent Technologies,' arguing that humanity lacks sufficient progress in guiding development.

In his encyclical Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo XIV outlined five considerations regarding artificial intelligence, emphasizing that Intelligent Technologies must remain directed toward the common good rather than serving only a privileged few.
Decisions affecting human Life, freedom, and the use of force must remain under human oversight, The Pope stressed, adding that no machine should ever choose whether to take human Life.
Encouraging global action, The Pope urged States meeting in Geneva to ban lethal autonomous weapons, noting that Intelligent Technologies must be 'disarmed' to ensure ethical use.

Shared standards and independent oversight are necessary to guide future development, The Pope argued, noting humanity's responsibility to 'guide, change, and, when necessary, reject' dangerous Applications.
title: Pope says ‘most urgent’ challenge facing AI race is need for institutional ethical framework

summary: On Thursday, 31-year-old Ashland resident Daniel Jones appeared in court charged with the double homicide of his father, Pipo Nguyen-Duy, and stepmother, Tran Thi Phong, in Oberlin, Ohio. A judge set his bond at $3 million.

Police discovered the two victims dead from multiple gunshot wounds at their South Pleasant Street home on Wednesday morning, shortly after officers responded to a vehicle fire at the Oberlin College campus. Jones was located at a nearby resident's home.

Prosecutor Zachary Simonoff said in court that Jones identified himself as Asia Nguyen-Duy, claimed he was "escaping a cult," and admitted he "killed his family." Officers found two people dead from gunshot wounds with blood throughout the house, Simonoff said.

Oberlin College President Carmen Twillie Ambar released a statement mourning the "devastating loss" of Nguyen-Duy, a professor of studio art and photography since 1998. The case will be presented to a grand jury in Lorain County Common Pleas Court.

While the motive remains under investigation, Simonoff noted police contacted Jones' mother in Oregon, who stated her son is "psychotic and needs medication." Jones did not enter a plea on Thursday and bore visible facial and hand injuries.
title: Suspect in Killings of Oberlin Professor, Wife Held on $3 Million Bond

summary: On Thursday, Former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi , D-Calif., criticized New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed over their views on Israel, calling their positions "wrong."
The exchange occurs amid ongoing debates within the Democratic Party regarding Israel, particularly following the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks and the subsequent war in Gaza.

El-Sayed has faced scrutiny for describing Israel's war in Gaza as "genocide" and characterizing military actions as "bloodthirsty," while Mamdani has questioned support for states privileging one religion over others.
Pelosi responded that these positions are "more than concerning" and do not reflect the views of Democrats in Congress, stating that members would disassociate themselves from such rhetoric.
Running against Republican Mike Rogers for a Senate seat in a state Trump carried in 2024, El-Sayed has rejected claims that criticism of Israel is antisemitic, citing a commitment to Jewish safety.
title: Nancy Pelosi Criticizes Mamdani and El-Sayed Over Their Positions on Israel

summary: Pop star Olivia Rodrigo wore a shirt reading "Dr. Amy Acton for Governor" during her Thursday, Oct. 29 concert at the Schottenstein Center in Columbus, displaying support for the Democratic gubernatorial candidate.

Rodrigo's endorsement follows a controversial campaign ad from Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy featuring Acton's estranged mother, Donna Arthur, who called her daughter a "liar" while urging voters to reject her.
Critics including Acton's brother Philip Stearns and Republican Governor Mike DeWine rebuked the ad for exploiting her childhood abuse at 12 years old, drawing bipartisan condemnation.
Acton's campaign shared photos on social media, writing " Ohio loves you." Rodrigo also encouraged concertgoers to vote, having previously raised $20 million for women's charities.
Voters head to the polls on Tuesday, Nov. 3 to decide the race. Recent polling shows Acton with a seven-point lead over Ramaswamy in the closely watched gubernatorial contest.
title: Olivia Rodrigo shows support for Amy Acton at Columbus concert
